key_insight: For single-hidden-layer ReLU networks, integrating over regions defined by activation breakpoints yields correct PDE-loss gradients that standard sampling can miss even with arbitrarily many points.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-aware integration can make neural PDE training more reliable when losses depend on spatial gradients, as in Deep Ritz and first-order PINNs.
method: Partition the domain along ReLU breaking hyperplanes using Sutherland–Hodgman clipping.
Assemble the energy in matrix–vector form for vectorized neuron interactions.
Introduce Conforming Monte Carlo and two stochastic training strategies to reduce complexity.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on two-dimensional domains recover optimal PDE solutions that standard stochastic sampling and other tested quadrature methods fail to capture.
watch_item: The framework targets single-hidden-layer networks, and geometric partitioning may become costly as neuron count or spatial dimension increases.
paper_title: Exact Integration of ReLU-type Neural Networks for Solving PDEs
